 Most animals inside Stanislaus wildlife center killed in fire
 By
 Richard Ramos 
 Richard Ramos 
 Web Producer, CBS Sacramento 
 Richard Ramos is a web producer for CBS Sacramento who was born and raised in Sacramento. He graduated with a BA in Journalism from CSUS.
 Read Full Bio 
 Richard Ramos 
 Updated on: November 18, 2026 / 10:42 PM PST 
 / CBS Sacramento
 Add CBS News on Google 
 Most animals inside the Stanislaus Wildlife Care Center in Hughson were killed in a fire on Wednesday evening, officials said.
 A Hughson Fire Department official told CBS News Sacramento that the fire was likely caused by an electrical issue. It was not immediately clear whether that involved downed power lines during Wednesday's storm or a separate issue.
 The Modesto Fire Department said around 7 p.m. that it had a crew assisting Hughson Fire with the fully involved structure fire along Geer Road.
 Donna Burt, the facility's executive director, said no people were inside the building at the time of the fire and noted that the roof of the building had collapsed. She said a neighbor to the facility notified her when flames were spotted on the building's roof. 
 Burt said firefighters called the building "a total loss" and told CBS News Sacramento that all animals that were inside the facility were likely dead.
 Fire officials confirmed at least 40 animals were dead. A CBS News Sacramento crew at the scene observed crews pulling two snakes and a turtle from the fire. Burt noted there were also some animals in outdoor cages that should be safe.
 The facility cares for injured and orphaned wildlife until they are ready to be released back out into their natural environments, Burt said. She added that many of them were resident animals who had spent years at the facility.
 "So far this year, we have taken in just short of 2,600 animals," Burt said.
